title: Hyperposition H4 Clay-Native Typed Semantic Firebreaks
summary: H4 refines HYP-RC3 for the owner-fixed Clay-native FRANK target. One Clay semantic language should compile into multiple non-interchangeable semantic failure domains (fact/observation/activation/proposal/form/authority/effect) with explicit trusted casts, operation-specific Origin–Selector–Basis witnesses, ancestry-bound revocation and compact hot-path lowering. Visible tags alone are not a trusted boundary.
key_evidence: H4 six-domain hypergraph cascade containment proxy
C6 typed-vs-untyped simple homoiconic negative control
key_negative_results: textual FACT/TEXT tags did not outperform untyped simple C6 proxy
typed firebreaks do not eliminate cognitive propagation
coverage and metadata overhead are nonzero
record provenance != selector integrity != origin authority
open_questions: Do runtime-enforced semantic casts contain real FRANK/ClayGraph multi-stage attacks?
What minimal semantic-domain lattice is sufficient?
What is live cast/dependency witness coverage?
Can packed handles meet target p99/cache budgets?
Does full Clay-native 4B adaptation reduce translation cost without increasing common-mode semantic failure?
